Create a Skat player

Source: R/players.R
sk_player.Rd

Players are strategy objects that, given a legal set of moves and the visible game context, choose a card to play. Three built-in strategies are provided.

Usage

sk_player(
  strategy = c("random", "heuristic", "mcts"),
  n_sims = 200,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

Arguments

strategy

One of "random", "heuristic", or "mcts".

  • "random": chooses uniformly among legal moves.

  • "heuristic": greedy rules – take the trick with the cheapest card that beats it when the trick is worth taking, otherwise shed the lowest-value card.

  • "mcts": determinized Monte Carlo search (see sk_mcts_move()).

n_sims

For "mcts", the number of determinized playouts per decision. Ignored otherwise. Defaults to 200.

call

The calling environment, used for error reporting.

Value

An object of class sk_player: a list with elements strategy (character) and n_sims (integer).

See also

sk_choose() to ask a player for a move.

Other player functions: sk_choose(), sk_mcts_move()

Examples

sk_player("heuristic")
#> <sk_player>: heuristic
sk_player("mcts", n_sims = 500)
#> <sk_player>: mcts (500 sims)
